key_insight: NereidVLA transfers knowledge of underwater objects and spatial relationships into language-guided 3D navigation. It first learns marine scene understanding without paired robot-motion data, then adapts that knowledge using expert trajectories.
problem_solved: Underwater robots must translate visual cues and language instructions into movement, but marine vision-language datasets rarely include corresponding robot trajectories.
method: Train Sea2Know on approximately two million marine examples to learn target grounding, spatial relationships, and scene structure.
Learn marine spatial knowledge without paired robot-motion supervision.
Adapt this knowledge using expert trajectories for language-conditioned 3D navigation; further training details are unavailable in the truncated abstract.
impact: The approach offers a way to reuse marine vision-language data when robot-motion demonstrations are scarce. It could help practitioners develop underwater navigation systems, although the provided abstract includes no performance results.
visual_elements: Two-stage pipeline: marine examples → Sea2Know spatial understanding → trajectory adaptation → NereidVLA navigation.
Underwater scene with labeled targets and spatial relationships, such as above, behind, and near.
Language instruction connected to a robot's 3D path through an underwater environment.
Data contrast graphic: approximately two million marine examples versus limited paired robot trajectories.
paper_title: NereidVLA: Learning to Understand and Navigate the Underwater World
paper_authors: Chenjie Zhao, Zhiliang Zhu, Quan Chen, Yuquan Xue, Xingxue Shi
